projects.description: Investment simulation: USD 1 million mandate combining adaptive risk architecture, investment-committee governance, and a decision-focused postmortem.

highlights.text: Led an eight-person desk through a USD 1 million StockTrak mandate, combining systematic factor selection with discretionary macro overlays informed by Project GANET research across AI, defence, financials, and defensive retail.

Protected capital during the 2 April tariff shock by activating the Section 5 override, moving into cash and inverse-ETF hedges, and containing the trough at -6.44% versus SPY at -11.72%, a 528-basis-point downside advantage.

Maintained IPS compliance by capping positions at 25% single-name limits, running weekly drift checks, and rebalancing sleeves across Foundation (~1.0 beta), Growth (1.1), Crisis (0.0), and Ceasefire (0.6) regime overlays.

Re-risked after the crisis window using an explicit April playbook rather than discretionary drift, finishing the mandate at -4.37% with 0.63 beta while preserving committee accountability through trade logs and bi-weekly decision diaries.
The behavioural audit exposed a 28.6% win rate and losses held roughly twice as long as winners; converted the findings into new position-sizing and exit rules.

Defended the strategy through a 2,600-word investment-committee memo and 20-slide oral defence, scoring 422/430 overall across architecture and logs, strategy and reporting, and the client postmortem.

projects.name: BWC Quantitative Portfolio Audit Engine
projects.description: Research prototype: reproducible Python decision-support stack built to audit the BWC simulation portfolio without connecting analysis code to live execution.

highlights.text: Built a reproducible Python 3.13 research environment with uv and PEP 517, implementing Fama-French three-factor OLS, Black-Litterman allocation, and Kelly sizing for portfolio diagnostics.
Reduced end-of-day analysis to sub-second pivots by normalising Polygon, yfinance, Alpaca, and FRED feeds into DuckDB with Polars and reusable market-regime labels.
Stress-tested 10,000 Monte Carlo paths with Cornish-Fisher VaR, reporting 5% VaR of -2.56%, Sortino 3.49, Calmar 6.34, and Jensen alpha 0.686; kept the model firewalled from live execution.
Made the audit operable through a Typer CLI for dashboard, backtest, and environment checks, plus Streamlit and Plotly views that exposed regime, attribution, and risk evidence to the team.
Hardened the toolchain with pre-commit checks, Ruff, Bandit, Deptry, MkDocs, Doppler-managed secrets, and immutable Appwrite snapshots so results remained reviewable and reproducible.
